## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Treatment Product
where: TreatmentProductRepository (uses), src/persistence/repositories.ts, component persistence

=====SOURCE-END=====

### B

=====SOURCE-END=====

response.rationale: These are two different concepts that are related to each other. A Treatment Product is a catalogue item: the persistence layer keeps them as `TreatmentProductRecord` in `TreatmentProductRepository`, and `TreatmentService.addProduct` and `TreatmentService.listProducts` manage them. A Treatment is an event tied to one hive, which is why `HarvestService` looks them up with `this.treatments.findByHive(hiveId)` in `TreatmentRepository`. `HarvestService` uses both: it calls `TreatmentRepository.findByHive` and, separately, `TreatmentProductRepository.findById`. That fits a treatment pointing to the product it uses, so a treatment applies a product rather than being one. They have separate repositories and are used in different ways, so they are not the same thing under two names.
